A razor-thin line of brilliant blue atmosphere rims the planet's curve, glowing against the black of space, fading to soft haze toward the terminator.
A blazing sunrise breaks over the planet's limb in a fan of gold and white light, the terminator a sharp divide between glowing day and dark night.
A glowing green auroral ring crowns the night-side pole, rippling curtains of light visible from orbit against the dark curve of the world below.
Storm lightning flickers in blue-white bursts across sunlit cloud-tops near the terminator, brief silent flashes illuminating towering anvil formations from within their shadowed depths.
A deep sunset-orange band saturates the terminator line, the atmosphere bending light into rich amber and red as the sun slips behind the limb.
A hazy violet-purple atmosphere glow wraps the entire visible limb, diffuse and dreamlike, bleeding into the darkness of space with no sharp edge to find.
The bright crescent of a sunlit limb blazes against absolute black, a slim arc of white-gold atmosphere curving away at both horns into shadow.
Thick banded atmosphere layers stack in parallel arcs along the limb, each band a different shade — pale blue, white, gold — like rings of compressed sky.
Airglow shimmers in a ghostly green sheet just above the dark side's surface, a thin luminous layer separate from the stars, hanging silent over the night.
The day-night terminator sweeps in a clean curving line across the surface, half the world burning in yellow sunlight, half swallowed entirely in cold black shadow.
A deep-red atmospheric halo bleeds around the dark limb during eclipse, the planet's own air bending the sun's reddened light into a glowing ruby ring.
High cirrus clouds catch the last sunlight just above the terminator, their thin white streaks blazing brilliant orange while the surface beneath them sinks into darkness.
A ragged terminator breaks across mountain ranges, the high peaks still catching full sunlight in bright dots while deep valleys below vanish into premature night.
A dual-toned limb glows where blue upper atmosphere transitions sharply to a white troposphere band, the two layers stacked in clean horizontal stripes along the curve.
Noctilucent clouds glow electric blue far above the dark terminator, thin rippled sheets of ice crystal lit by a sun already set below the horizon.
A pale sodium-yellow airglow ring encircles the entire night hemisphere, a chemical luminescence too faint to see from the surface but vivid against the black of orbit.
The limb atmosphere glows a deep teal near the poles, sunlight scattering through thicker cold-air columns, different in color from the white-blue of the equatorial haze.
A massive hurricane eye is visible at the terminator edge, its spiral bands half-lit in brilliant white, the other half in shadow and flickering with lightning.
The thin atmosphere of a high-altitude desert world barely glows at the limb, a faint reddish arc fragile and nearly invisible against the surrounding star-filled darkness.
A brilliant green flash pulses at the very moment the sun clears the limb, a magnified atmospheric optical effect blazing for one breathless second before fading.
Volcanic ash clouds billow above the terminator, stained amber and brown, catching oblique sunlight and casting long dark shadows back across the cloud-tops behind them.
The soft pink glow of a carbon-dioxide-rich atmosphere rims the limb, a Martian-toned arc of dusty rose light curving gently across the face of the dark.
A tidal-locked world shows a permanent terminator frozen in place, the day side blazing white-hot, the night side utterly dark, with a narrow habitable glow between.
Thin wisps of high atmosphere trail off the limb into space like pale blue smoke, the topmost layers too tenuous to hold together, bleeding out into vacuum.
A second faint atmospheric arc hovers above the main limb glow, a detached haze layer floating higher, creating a double-line effect along the sunlit curve of the world.
